Extremely unoptimized—even on recommended specs I am running a system that fully meets the recommended specifications, but the performance is completely unacceptable. This game is incredibly unoptimized across the board.
Changing the graphics settings makes absolutely no difference. Whether you drop everything to the lowest preset or push it higher, the poor performance remains exactly the same. The most glaring issue is how it runs on Intel hardware. It is severely unoptimized for Intel users, leading to constant frame drops and a nearly unplayable experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out issues with platform compatibility, specifically noting a lack of proper Steam Deck support or login failures on Linux.

citations.review_text: No steam deck support is just terrible

This game doesnt let me login on linux and ive never had this issue for a live service or steam cloud save game on linux. the login screen does not work on any proton version (og proton, ge, hotfix, cachyos, dw, experimental) and only lets me log onto a guest account (none of my progress from playing before on windows with a once human account and steam account doesnt sync either, says profile not found); thats unacceptable for a live service game, so i dont reccommned this game if you game on linux since there are much better games you can spend your time with anyway that actually cloud/server-side save or can be run locally. out of all games ive played on linux, this has been the only game that hasnt had a login option (it logs onto guest account so no progress is saved) plus a couple of the times i tried launching the game it crashed my gpu drivers. also this is an authentication level issue on the server side since when i click "exit" out of character creator when entering game on guest account since it didnt load my data properly, for a split second a frame loads of my character i created on my official once human account inside the game world before transitioning to the main menu so this is definitely a backend issue, and ive tried both the official launcher and steam launcher vers of the game and same reproducible results. my first install of the game was on steam with windows but after that i switched to linux with the same steam account and steam ID. the data exists on the server but there is clearly some sort of authentication issue going on here since the authentication process is being blocked on linux while i remember it working on windows. Trying it on linux i reinstalled this 4 times (over 400gb btw) to try test workarounds and tried deleting prefixes, repaired files and nothing worked.  imo only play this if your bound to windows cuz of ring 0 anticheat games otherwise dont bother. dont know why this is gold on proton db when it fails to even log yo…

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the early game features an overwhelming amount of menus, tasks, and confusing systems, making it difficult to figure out what items do or how mechanics work.

citations.review_text:
The game in itself is quite fun, but it really doesn't know what it's supposed to be. The militaristic post apocalypse vibe is fun and you can get quite immersed in farming and base building. But then that gets ruined when you see people running about in bikini's and pirate costumes, who build sparkling clean bases with paid cosmetics that they really don't belong in this type of scenario.

The game itself is quite difficult to get into if you're just starting and don't have someone walking you through it. There are just far too many miscellaneous or potentially useful things (which aren't really explained if you should be hoarding them of disassembling them). At the start you'll find your inventory cluttered with all sorts of junk. I tried for a while but got bored of trying to learn what everything did. After 50 hours of playing I can honestly say that I still don't know what most of the things in this game do.

When it comes to paid cosmetics, even that is overcomplicated to the extreme. There are at least 15 different currencies (Not even joking) for paying for things in the cosmetic shops. I considered buying some things, but was turned away because I really didn't know how to get the currency that I needed for the specific cosmetic pack that I was wanting. Nothing about it was clear. They could fix this by removing 90% of the currencies and just have one for in game purchases off of shopkeepers etc (Free to play), and one for the cosmetic shop (Pay)

The cosmetic shop prices are insane as well. I was looking at purchasing the glass walls so i could decorate my base a bit more, only to see it was nearly £50 for the glass cosmetic pack. I get that 5-10% of the player base fund the entire game with their disposable incomes and lapping up the high price tags, but for the average gamer that's just crazy.

The game is beautiful graphics wise, it plays smoothly and the gameplay is fun. It's just a shame that they didn't stick to one theme, instead of having a…

This game is really fun to play and the visuals are great. The early game can be confusing as there are so many tasks to follow and a lot of pages in the menu. Despite being a bit confusing in that sense, the game is enjoyable.

Got into it a while ago, didn't quite understand it and the GUI was pretty weird at first. It looked a lot like a pubg mobile type system, despite the decent guides on Youtube I definitely had some struggles learning what certain things did, how certain bosses/dungeons worked or the meaning of some icons on the gui which we're not as thoroughly explained as I guess I needed it to be.

I came back a week ago and I feel as if there are a lot of changes that made the game simpler to understand and make you realize how insanely good the game actually is easily letting you sink hours of playtime in it because it really takes the best out of everything. Want a big world to explore? Different maps? Into  base building? With friends? Clans? PvP? Not your thing? Try PvE with Dungeon like gamemodes, Bosses, with friends or alone and unique build making catering everything exactly to how YOU want to play the game. I could truly go on and on, I don't know if I'm plain old stupid or if other people had issues figuring the game out aswell, But I have to say once you learn how to play and progress fast the game really takes ahold of you.

Good game, fun, but so COMPLEX and confusing. I didn't understand anything from the main story, and you need to do a PhD to learn and understand the mechanics of this game, there are a lot of things to learn and master, it is really difficult and it takes time to learn

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires managing gear repair mechanics.

citations.review_text:
While the cosmic-horror and surreal world in an apocalyptic setting is intriguing, it's not enough to keep going.
The voice acting is very hit and miss and not everything (especially some side quests) are not voiced and there's translation issues with the subtitles where the spoken dialogue and subtitles don't line up and it be annoying and detracts from the immersion of the story.
The Narrative delivery, character writing, and pacing of the quests feel generic as all get out and makes the story feel shoehorned in and secondary to the survival gameplay. I would have liked a happy balance of both.
The difficulty balancing is terrible. I played on Easy mode, as I'm more interested in the worldbuilding and story elements then the survival aspects and there were times where the combat was clunky and incredibly brutal  and getting hit by zombie like creatures results in death after no less then 3 hits. Not to mention having to constantly keep up with repairing gear and persistantly engaging in the survival elements, it brought my engagement and interest to progress the story content come to a screeching halt.

Overall: if your big into the survival and building gameplay elements in these type of games, this is for you. If your looking for a unique and engaging story with quality delivery, decent combat gameplay and passable voice acting and balanced difficulty, this isn't it. In short: I picked this game up multiple time and have come to the conclusion, this isn't for me.

[h2]Great base building, but the survival grind will test your actual sanity.[/h2]

If you are looking for an open-world survival shooter to play with a small group of friends, Once Human has some surprisingly solid bones. However, it also makes a few design choices that feel like they actively want to disrespect your time.

[h3]The Good[/h3] (Why we stuck around):
[list]
[*] Snappy Combat: The controls and aiming feel incredibly responsive.
[*] Top-Tier Base Building: If you enjoyed Fallout 76's camp system, you'll feel right at home here. The absolute best feature? You can freely move objects around your base after placing them. It's a game-changer for builders.
[*] Server Costs: At the time of playing, I was able to rent a custom 4-player server for under $3 a month. It is hard to beat that value for a private co-op experience.
[*] Progression: The leveling and tech tree are well-paced and satisfying.
[/list]

[h3]The Bad[/h3] (Why it gets frustrating):
[list]
[*] The "Sanity" Mechanic: This is just a dumb mechanic. It adds unnecessary frustration, traps you in miserable death loops, and causes excessive damage to your gear. It is the opposite of fun.
[*] The Survival Tedium: Food and water drain way too fast. Combine that with punishing gear durability, and you are forced into a constant loot-farming loop just to keep your equipment repaired.
[*] Missing Basics: We have this great building system, but there are no ramps in the building menu? Make it make sense.
[*] Narrative & UI Flaws: The story and characters are very "meh." Voice acting is limited, and for the unvoiced missions, the text flies by so fast you literally cannot read it. Also, quest levels are frequently mismatched with the level of the area they are in.
[*] Absurd Microtransactions: Cosmetics are entirely too expensive. I am not paying $40+ for a cosmetic base set when I can spend $20 on a complete indie game that includes far more building parts right out of the box.
[/list]…

Nice game for those who love looter shooter, survival and tons of crafting.
Worst thing in game is repairing mechanic. So why all equipment must be repaired? Devs maby delete this mechanic?

Lets start off by saying that I have had an over all great experience with the game. At points it feels like Lovecraft mixed with SCP. The world is big with plenty to explore. The weapons and armor upgrades work well. The base building here is some of my favorite when it comes to base building games. While I do recommend this game, there is a massive BUT. The monetization here and lootbox mechanics are some of the worst I have ever seen. I thought WoW, Diablo, and Call of Duty were bad but Once Human is on a completely different level! An average skin in those other games are around $20ish? Here you are looking at closer to $100-$200 due to the lootbox nature of it. 

If you are looking for a fun game to build bases, grind levels and gear, and explore creepy environments this is the game for you. I would avoid the cash shop if you want cool skins. At least there is no pay to win. Well not that I have noticed at least.

Once Human fell under my radar and I wish I had found it sooner. It has a good progression but lacks a good quest tracking ability. The building system works very well except for the lack of being able to build a remote second base for oil and stardust collection. The cosmetics are very expensive, so a way to collect more of them internal to the game would be useful. Overall a great game, definitely recommend, and it is free to play.
